cases.input: One onboarding Service has EU in-house and APAC outsourced realization bindings.
cases.expect: One Service identity and outcome specification remain stable; provider parties and implementations are effective bindings.

cases.input: One identity-verification Service is exposed through two endpoints and a usage-priced offering.
cases.expect: Endpoints and price remain external while Service identity is unchanged.

cases.input: An internal platform Service is accountable and observed but is not requestable and has no offering row.
cases.expect: The Service definition is valid; catalogue membership is not an identity invariant.

cases.input: A Service is marked requestable but no external offering row can be resolved.
cases.expect: The candidate is held for catalogue coverage; it does not create a second offering master.

cases.input: One external offering bundles two Service definitions and is later withdrawn.
cases.expect: Both Service identities survive; offering composition and withdrawal remain catalogue-owned.

cases.input: An API endpoint is replaced with no change to outcome consumer scope or accountability.
cases.expect: No new Service identity; only the realization binding changes.

cases.input: An external provider replaces an internal provider for the same outcome, consumer scope and accountable role.
cases.expect: No new Service identity; provider incumbency and realization bindings are effective-dated.

cases.input: A technical endpoint has uptime metadata but no consumer outcome or accountable-provider role type.
cases.expect: It is not accepted as a Service.

cases.input: A workflow is presented as a Service solely because it performs onboarding steps.
cases.expect: The workflow remains a process realization and cannot own Service identity.

cases.input: One observed latency breaches a target.
cases.expect: Observation and breach result remain external and do not mutate the Service definition.

cases.input: A consumer has an entitlement, two requests and one fulfilment for a Service offering.
cases.expect: Consumption is derived from external records and no Service Consumption root is minted.

cases.input: Service A requires version 2 of Service B only in region EU.
cases.expect: The owned dependency association remains directional, version-pinned, region-scoped and effective-dated without a public identifier.

cases.input: A Service depends on an already-identified platform capability.
cases.expect: The target is allowed when its external master is resolvable; the dependency does not master that capability.

cases.input: A Service Dependency directly targets an API endpoint.
cases.expect: Rejected: the endpoint is a realization target, not a Service Dependency target.

cases.input: A local dependency label is treated as globally canonical because it appears in this candidate.
cases.expect: Rejected: dependency labels are illustrative until an external vocabulary authority is approved.

cases.input: An SLA cannot reference the Service-definition key and its metrics are proposed for copying into WM-ACT-004.
cases.expect: Publication remains held; SLA terms and measurements are not absorbed.

cases.input: A Service is retired while historical subscriptions and cases remain.
cases.expect: Service and superseded bindings remain resolvable without accepting new consumption.

cases.input: A binding or dependency receives a new public business identifier from this contour.
cases.expect: Rejected: associations may have internal persistence keys only and EM-PRD-02 allocates no public identifier.

cases.input: A wording correction leaves outcome, consumer scope and accountability archetype unchanged.
cases.expect: The Service owner appends a monotonic contained revision under the same serviceId; no new root is created.

cases.input: A proposed revision changes the expected outcome and consumer scope materially.
cases.expect: It cannot be a revision; a successor Service identity is required under WM-ACT-004 authority.

cases.input: A realization binding is exposed by a public URI and independent lookup.
cases.expect: Rejected: bindings are available only through definition-scoped traversal and aggregate history.

cases.input: EU internal staff and APAC BPO staff fill the same accountable-provider archetype.
cases.expect: Sourcing mode and provider party do not change the role type or Service identity.

cases.input: A binding becomes effective using local realization-kind and scope labels without approved pinned vocabularies.
cases.expect: Publication is held; labels never re-key association records.

cases.input: A dependency becomes effective using an illustrative local type.
cases.expect: Publication is held until an approved pinned dependency-type vocabulary exists.

cases.input: A non-requestable internal Service has a fulfilment record for a party and no offering.
cases.expect: The view derives from Service, party and the owning external record with no null offering identity and no consumption root.

cases.input: An SLA references registryId plus serviceId and pins serviceVersionRef for revision-specific terms.
cases.expect: The join resolves the Service instance without copying SLA fields or allocating a new model identifier.

cases.input: A consumer can read the Service but not its confidential provider binding.
cases.expect: The provider reference is redacted under intersection semantics without confirming the hidden record exists.

cases.input: A definition-only internal Service becomes requestable with no outcome or consumer-scope change.
cases.expect: Service identity remains; catalogue applicability changes and publication is held until an offering row resolves.
